extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short fiction to Strange Horizons (speculative fiction magazine)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and production guidelines for authors of speculative short fiction seeking publication in the online magazine Strange Horizons, covering eligible material, formatting, rights, payment, and editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target genre
rubrics_metrics.description: We want: Speculative fiction, broadly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your story doesn't have a speculative element, or strong speculative-fiction sensibilities, it's probably not for us.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred and maximum length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We prefer stories under 5,000 words, but consider up to 10,000 words. The longer the story, the less likely we are to be interested. We can't consider stories much over the limit, not even as serials. We have no minimum wordcount; we consider short-short stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordcount measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: We determine story length by taking the word-processor wordcount and rounding up to the next highest 100 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously unpublished in English
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously unpublished in English—we buy first English rights, including audio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We will consider stories which have previously appeared in another language, but have never been published in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (gateway only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted through our Moksha submission gateway—no email or postal submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order to track stories correctly, we can only consider stories submitted through that form—no email or paper mail submissions. If you're having trouble submitting, email fiction@strangehorizons.com with subject 'QUERY: Your Question Topic'.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no re-submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No simultaneous or multiple submissions; no re-submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously or multiple stories at once from the same author are not acceptable. Stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons, even if they have been revised, will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: File types and basic formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send only RTF, DOC or DOCX files and try to stick to standard manuscript format as much as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't worry about font, font size, line spacing or indentation — our system automatically reformats submissions the way we like them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content
rubrics_metrics.description: Your cover letter can be minimal: generally, these should be short and list just a few of your most recent or most relevant publications or workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you've got life experience relevant to your story, please mention that. Cover letters shouldn't include plot synopses or pitches. See the sample cover letters page if concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment rate and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of 8¢/word USD, within 60 days of contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum payment is $60. We pay by check or PayPal according to the author's preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights purchased and reuse period
rubrics_metrics.description: We buy first-printing world exclusive English-language rights (including audio) for six (6) months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After that period, you are free to republish the story elsewhere. We hope you'll allow us to leave the story in our archives indefinitely after it's rotated off the main table of contents, but you have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional-market status
rubrics_metrics.description: SFWA officially considers us a professional market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment and status consistent with SFWA professional-market recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content preferences — themes, perspective, style
rubrics_metrics.description: Some particular things we love, or are interested in: Fiction from or about diverse perspectives and traditionally under-represented groups, written from a non-exoticizing and well-researched position; Unusual yet readable styles and inventive structures and narratives; Stories that address political issues in complex and nuanced ways, resisting oversimplification; Hypertext fiction (query first).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have hyperfiction, query us to discuss how to submit it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable language and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Profanity is fine. Sex or violence in a story should be artistically justified; no excessive gore. We welcome submissions from anywhere in the world, and British spellings are fine.

rubrics_metrics.name: What we will not consider — content/format exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Things we won't consider: Stories above 10,000 words, including serialized novels or novellas; Partial or incomplete stories; Unsolicited reprints of works previously published in English; Stories previously submitted to Strange Horizons; Multiple stories at once from the same author; Submissions sent to us and another venue simultaneously; Poetry or nonfiction (wrong department).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not send part of a story and ask us to request the rest later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and autoresponder policy
rubrics_metrics.description: We usually respond within a few weeks, but if you haven't heard from us within 40 days, please query immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We send an autoresponder message in response to every submission we receive. If you haven't received an autoresponse within 24 hours after submitting, please query immediately — missing an autoresponse usually means we have an incorrect email address for you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly submissions schedule and temporary closures
rubrics_metrics.description: To manage volume, we try a weekly schedule: We'll always reopen every Monday when the new issue is published. When we're open, there will be no daily cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the week, if and when the queue begins to significantly outstrip the reading, we'll close for the week to give ourselves room to catch up. This page will clearly indicate whether we're closed and when we'll be reopening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: After you submit a story, we strongly prefer you don't withdraw it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you withdraw a story, we won't consider any version of that story in the future. If you do need to withdraw a story, please send an email telling us that you need to withdraw, and let us know why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archive retention and author removal rights
rubrics_metrics.description: We hope you'll allow us to leave the story in our archives indefinitely after it's rotated off the main table of contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You have the right to remove your story from the archives at any time after one (1) year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission tracking and contact protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have any questions, write to fiction@strangehorizons.com with the word QUERY: at the beginning of your subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a few words to the subject line to indicate what you're querying about.
